title: 207. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Polynomial Inequalities Using Sign Charts
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a factored polynomial inequality by using sign analysis.
questions.question: Solve \((x+1)(x-3)>0\).
questions.explanation: The critical values are \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\). The product is positive when the two factors have the same sign. On \(x<-1\), both factors are negative, so the product is positive. On \(-1<x<3\), the factors have opposite signs, so the product is negative. On \(x>3\), both factors are positive, so the product is positive. Therefore the solution is \(x<-1\) or \(x>3\).
questions.hint: Find the values that make each factor zero, then test the sign of the product on the intervals.

questions.concept: Solving polynomial inequalities with two factors
questions.learningObjective: Solve a factored polynomial inequality and express the solution as a closed interval.
questions.question: Solve \((x-2)(x+4)\le0\).
questions.explanation: The critical values are \(x=-4\) and \(x=2\). The product is negative between the roots and equals zero at the roots. On \(-4<x<2\), the factors have opposite signs, so the product is negative. At \(x=-4\) and \(x=2\), the product is \(0\), which satisfies the inequality. Therefore the solution is \(-4\le x\le2\).
questions.hint: Determine where the product is negative, then include the endpoints where the product equals zero.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a cubic polynomial inequality by constructing a sign chart.
questions.question: Solve \(x(x-1)(x+2)>0\).
questions.explanation:
The critical values are \(x=-2\), \(x=0\), and \(x=1\). Testing the sign on each interval:
For \(x<-2\), all three factors are negative, so the product is negative.
For \(-2<x<0\), \(x+2>0\), \(x<0\), and \(x-1<0\), so the product is positive.
For \(0<x<1\), \(x+2>0\), \(x>0\), and \(x-1<0\), so the product is negative.
For \(x>1\), all three factors are positive, so the product is positive.
Therefore the solution is \(-2<x<0\) or \(x>1\).
questions.hint: Place the critical values on a number line and test the sign of each factor on every interval.

questions.concept: Polynomial inequalities with a repeated factor
questions.learningObjective: Solve a polynomial inequality containing a squared factor by using sign analysis.
questions.question: Solve \((x-1)^2(x+3)<0\).
questions.explanation: Since \((x-1)^2\) is always nonnegative and equals zero only at \(x=1\), it does not change the sign of the product except at \(x=1\). The product is negative exactly when \(x+3<0\), which gives \(x<-3\). At \(x=-3\), the product is \(0\), not less than \(0\). Therefore the solution is \(x<-3\).
questions.hint: A squared factor is nonnegative; determine where the remaining factor makes the product negative.

questions.concept: Polynomial inequalities with a repeated root at zero
questions.learningObjective: Solve a polynomial inequality involving a squared monomial factor.
questions.question: Solve \(x^2(x-2)\ge0\).
questions.explanation: The factor \(x^2\) is positive for all \(x\ne 0\) and equals zero at \(x=0\). For \(x<0\), \(x^2>0\) and \(x-2<0\), so the product is negative. For \(0<x<2\), the product is also negative. At \(x=0\), the product is \(0\), which satisfies \(x^2(x-2)\ge0\). At \(x=2\), the product is \(0\). For \(x>2\), the product is positive. Therefore the solution is \(x=0\) or \(x\ge2\).
questions.hint: Treat the squared factor separately and include the value where it equals zero.

questions.concept: Solving polynomial inequalities with three linear factors
questions.learningObjective: Solve a cubic polynomial inequality by testing intervals on a sign chart.
questions.question: Solve \((x+1)(x-2)(x-4)\le0\).
questions.explanation:
The critical values are \(x=-1\), \(x=2\), and \(x=4\). Testing the sign:
For \(x<-1\), all three factors are negative, so the product is negative.
For \(-1<x<2\), the product is positive.
For \(2<x<4\), the product is negative.
For \(x>4\), the product is positive.
The product equals zero at \(x=-1,2,4\). Therefore the solution is \(x\le-1\) or \(2\le x\le4\).
questions.hint: Use the critical values to divide the number line into intervals, then test the sign of the product on each interval.

questions.concept: Polynomial inequalities with a repeated factor and strict inequality
questions.learningObjective: Solve a polynomial inequality with a repeated factor by using sign analysis.
questions.question: Solve \((x+2)^2(x-1)>0\).
questions.explanation: The factor \((x+2)^2\) is nonnegative and equals zero at \(x=-2\). For \(x<-2\), \((x+2)^2>0\) and \(x-1<0\), so the product is negative. For \(-2<x<1\), the product is also negative. At \(x=-2\), the product is \(0\), which is not greater than \(0\). For \(x>1\), both factors are positive, so the product is positive. Therefore the solution is \(x>1\).
questions.hint: The squared factor never makes the product positive by itself; check where the other factor is positive.

questions.concept: Polynomial inequalities with a repeated factor and non-strict inequality
questions.learningObjective: Solve a polynomial inequality with a repeated factor and include zero endpoints correctly.
questions.question: Solve \((x-1)(x+2)^2(x-3)\ge0\).
questions.explanation: The factor \((x+2)^2\) is nonnegative and equals zero at \(x=-2\). The sign of the product is determined by \((x-1)(x-3)\) except at \(x=-2\), where the product is \(0\). The critical values are \(x=-2,1,3\). Testing intervals shows the product is nonnegative on \(x\le1\) and \(x\ge3\), and negative on \(1<x<3\). At \(x=1\) and \(x=3\), the product is \(0\), so these endpoints are included. Therefore the solution is \(x\le1\) or \(x\ge3\).
questions.hint: The squared factor is never negative; focus on the sign of the remaining factors and include all zeros.

questions.concept: Solving a cubic polynomial inequality from expanded form
questions.learningObjective: Solve an expanded cubic inequality by factoring and using a sign chart.
questions.question: Solve \(x^3-4x^2+x+6<0\).
questions.explanation:
Factor the cubic:
\[
x^3-4x^2+x+6=(x+1)(x-2)(x-3)
\]
The critical values are \(x=-1\), \(x=2\), and \(x=3\). Testing the sign:
For \(x<-1\), the product is negative.
For \(-1<x<2\), the product is positive.
For \(2<x<3\), the product is negative.
For \(x>3\), the product is positive.
Therefore the solution of \((x+1)(x-2)(x-3)<0\) is \(x<-1\) or \(2<x<3\).
questions.hint: Factor the cubic first, then test the sign of the product on the intervals determined by its roots.

questions.concept: Solving quartic polynomial inequalities by sign analysis
questions.learningObjective: Solve a quartic polynomial inequality by factoring into linear factors and using a sign chart.
questions.question: Solve \((x^2-4)(x^2-1)\ge0\).
questions.explanation:
Factor completely:
\[
(x^2-4)(x^2-1)=(x-2)(x+2)(x-1)(x+1)
\]
The critical values are \(x=-2,-1,1,2\). Testing the sign on each interval:
For \(x<-2\), all four factors are negative, so the product is positive.
For \(-2<x<-1\), the product is negative.
For \(-1<x<1\), the product is positive.
For \(1<x<2\), the product is negative.
For \(x>2\), the product is positive.
The product equals zero at \(x=-2,-1,1,2\). Therefore the solution is \(x\le-2\) or \(-1\le x\le1\) or \(x\ge2\).
questions.hint: Factor each quadratic as a difference of squares, then determine the sign of the product on the intervals between all four roots.
